questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you lose points by:

options.text: Exiting the vehicle one time to check your position.

questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each time you cross a line, you lose points.

questions.question: During exercises other than straight line backing, you can exit your vehicle to check its position no more than:
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check your position during the test. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can only look once. For other exercises, you can look twice.

questions.question: When preparing to enter traffic, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Be ready for your vehicle to accelerate slowly, especially if it is loaded.
Make sure you can completely cross traffic without getting in other drivers' way.
Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will make room for you. Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle. Know that your vehicle will accelerate slower if it is loaded. Make sure you can cross traffic completely without getting in other drivers' way.

questions.question: You can be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you:

options.text: Are a permanent resident of the United States.
Have never been convicted of a felony.
Have been committed to a mental institution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been committed to a mental institution.
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazmat endorsement if you are not a U.S. permanent resident, you gave up your citizenship, you were convicted of certain crimes, you have mental health issues, or the TSA says you are a security risk.

questions.question: When other vehicles have trouble seeing you at dawn or dusk, you can be more visible by:
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, or in snow or rain, turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey all traffic signs and signals only if other traffic is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey all traffic signs and signals only if other traffic is present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road test. Wear your safety belt. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws at all times. Do not have an accident or moving violation.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail due to:

options.text: Driving uphill for long periods of time.

questions.explanation: Hydraulic brakes fail when hydraulic pressure is lost. Brakes also fade when you use them too much on long downhill slopes.

questions.question: A vehicle stopped at a green light may show that the driver:
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or who are very tired can be dangerous. Stopping at a green light is a sign the driver may be impaired.

questions.question: Brakes may get out of adjustment if:
questions.explanation: Brakes get out of adjustment quickly when they overheat from heavy use. Check your brakes often.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes must use mechanical force to stay engaged.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy
When you are carrying a passenger
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet, snowy, or icy
questions.explanation: A retarder slows your vehicle and reduces brake wear. But it can cause your wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn off the retarder when the road is wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction of the turn
Look in the opposite direction of the turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction of the turn
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers look in the direction they are turning. Even if a driver doesn't signal, their body movement and eye direction can show that they plan to turn.

questions.question: When going downhill, shift into a lower gear:

options.text: As you pick up speed going downhill
Near the bottom of the hill

questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before going downhill. Shifting to a lower gear at high speed can damage the transmission and cause you to lose engine braking power. Choose a speed based on the hill's steepness, length, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: To make night driving easier, you should:

options.text: Dim your instrument panel lights as much as possible while still reading the gauges
Not take a nap before driving
Use only your low beam headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Dim your instrument panel lights as much as possible while still reading the gauges
questions.explanation: A bright interior makes it hard to see outside at night. Turn off the interior light and set your instrument lights to the lowest level that lets you read the gauges easily.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: The truck will have no brakes
The truck should only be driven slowly
The truck will still have brakes
The truck will have no brakes on the left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: If you realize you may be running late, you should:

options.text: Use flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way
Drive safely and arrive when you arrive

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive safely and arrive when you arrive
questions.explanation: Stay calm and accept delays. Rushing leads to dangerous driving. Plan extra time into your trip to avoid stress about being late.

questions.question: On a leaf spring, the leaves:
questions.explanation: Check your suspension for broken or missing leaves on leaf springs. Broken leaves are dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must not be driven.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
Someone driving a rental truck without experience with trucks
A driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person operating a pickup truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pickup truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazardous. This includes drivers with ice on windshields, those with large items blocking windows, and those unfamiliar with a rental truck's limited visibility. Simply driving a pickup truck is not inherently hazardous.

questions.question: Blocking a load:

options.text: Is dangerous and should never be done
Can only be done in dry weather

questions.explanation: Block cargo to prevent it from moving during transport. Shifting cargo can make steering and handling difficult for the driver.

questions.question: If a tire fails, the driver should:

options.text: Keep one hand on the wheel and wave to other drivers with the other hand

questions.explanation: Using the brakes after a tire failure can cause you to lose control. Avoid braking unless you need to avoid a crash. Let the vehicle slow down, then brake gently, pull off the road, and stop.

questions.question: Vehicles with dual air brake systems:

options.text: Keep full air pressure in the brakes even when the engine is off.
Keep some air pressure in the brakes when the engine is off.
Must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
Do not need time to build air pressure before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must run the engine to build enough air pressure for the brakes to work.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, you must wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: Fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns must be kept by carriers for:
questions.explanation: If you operate a commercial vehicle across state lines, it must be registered under the International Registration Plan (IRP) and International Fuel Tax Agreement (IFTA). These programs collect registration fees and fuel taxes based on where you drive. Carriers must keep mileage and fuel records that support IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns for four years.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Never use the brake pedal if your spring brakes are activated. Applying both spring pressure and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: If you feel sleepy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving to finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Pull off the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel sleepy while driving, you must stop and get sleep. Trying to fight tiredness is dangerous and causes many fatal crashes. Energy pills are not safe because they may keep you awake but will not make you more alert. When the pills wear off, you will be even more tired than before.

questions.question: After the engine is started, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle starts moving.

questions.explanation: After the engine starts, all warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately. The charging circuit light, oil light, coolant light, and Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) light should all go off.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern if passengers are not getting off.
Should not be on the road.
Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether you see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind the bus, and the bus can block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: When driving, hold the steering wheel:

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel.
With both hands at the top of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands placed on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When driving:

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Use turn signals only if there are vehicles nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: It is important to communicate with other drivers on the road. Signal before turning or changing lanes, even if you do not see other vehicles nearby.

questions.question: If a tire rim is damaged, it should be:

options.text: Placed on the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe to use.

questions.question: During the steering box portion of the vehicle inspection, you should not:

options.text: Check that the steering box is securely mounted.
Check that the steering box is free of leaks.
Look for missing bolts in the steering box.
Assume all cotter keys are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume all cotter keys are present.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that the steering box is securely mounted. Look for missing nuts, bolts, and cotter keys. Check for power steering fluid leaks and damage to power steering hoses.

questions.question: A driver will lose their CDL for at least one year for:

options.text: Leaving the scene of an accident involving a CMV.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leaving the scene of an accident involving a CMV.
questions.explanation: If you leave the scene of an accident involving a CMV, you will lose your CDL for at least one year.

questions.question: When checking the springs during a vehicle inspection, do all of the following except:

options.text: Check that torsion springs are not damaged.

questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, check for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Also check for broken or distorted coil springs. If the vehicle has torsion bars or torque arms, make sure they are not damaged and are mounted securely. Do not glue cracked springs.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a BAC of 0.04 percent or higher. Operating a CMV while under the influence of alcohol will cause you to lose your license for at least one year.

questions.question: Distracted drivers may be:

options.text: Not talking to anyone else in their vehicles.

questions.explanation: You can tell a driver is distracted if they are drifting within a lane or across lane dividers, traveling at inconsistent speeds, using a cell phone or looking at a map, eating, or talking to passengers.

questions.question: You should always use at least ____ to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Any cargo, no matter how small, must use a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving skills test, you will be evaluated on your gear usage. You should not:

options.text: Select a gear that does not rev the engine.
Forget to shift through an intersection.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine. Avoid grinding and clashing gears. Do not shift while turning or going through intersections.

questions.question: When backing, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to get out of the way of other drivers.
Try not to use your mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing a large CMV is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. If you must back up, use a helper when possible.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: Scan the road ahead to spot hazards early. Plan how you will handle potential dangers if they become unsafe.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has a single air brake system, but uses two sets of controls.
Has one air brake system for each side of the truck.
Has two brakes for each wheel.
Has two separate air brake systems, but uses a single set of controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems, but uses a single set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of brake controls. One system operates the rear axle brakes. The other system operates the front axle brakes.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the correct speed. Then push in the clutch, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Brake harder than in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
Brake with less force than in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS. The ABS system works automatically to prevent wheel lockup.

questions.question: If your vehicle's ABS stops working while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Use your parking brake to stop.

questions.explanation: Your vehicle's basic brakes still work without ABS. Continue to drive and brake normally.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Supports the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load at the correct distance from the driver.
Maintains a safe distance between your vehicle and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supports the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Damage to the suspension is dangerous.

questions.question: When should you use your headlights on high beam?

options.text: Headlights are not necessary at night.
Headlights provide better light than sunlight.
Use high beam whenever it is safe and legal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use high beam whenever it is safe and legal.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night for better visibility when safe and legal. Switch to low beam within 500 feet of approaching vehicles to avoid blinding other drivers.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes
A part in the braking unit that allows air to flow

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device in an air brake system. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: Why should you avoid eating while driving?

options.text: It is encouraged on long trips.
It distracts your attention from driving.
You must watch the cargo at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts your attention from driving.
questions.explanation: Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. These activities take your attention away from the road.

questions.question: When backing a truck, what mirrors should you use?
questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors frequently when backing to watch for hazards. Have a helper watch your blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for an escape route like an escape ramp or open field.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are near.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.

questions.explanation: When making a turn during your driving test, check traffic in all directions and always use your turn signal.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what should you do with engine belts?

options.text: Inspect them only if they look frayed.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check engine belts for tightness and excessive wear.
